{{Short description|Theorem describing tensor behavior}}
In [[general relativity]], the '''peeling theorem''' describes the asymptotic behavior of the [[Weyl tensor]] as one goes to [http://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/null_infinity null infinity]. Let <math>\gamma</math> be a [[null geodesic]] in a [[spacetime]] <math>(M, g_{ab})</math> from a point p to null infinity, with [[affine parameter]] <math>\lambda</math>. Then the theorem states that, as <math>\lambda</math> tends to infinity:

:<math>C_{abcd} = \frac{C^{(1)}_{abcd}}{\lambda}+\frac{C^{(2)}_{abcd}}{\lambda^2}+\frac{C^{(3)}_{abcd}}{\lambda^3}+\frac{C^{(4)}_{abcd}}{\lambda^4}+O\left(\frac{1}{\lambda^5}\right)</math>

where <math>C_{abcd}</math> is the Weyl tensor, and [[abstract index notation]] is used. Moreover, in the [[Petrov classification]], <math>C^{(1)}_{abcd}</math> is type N, <math>C^{(2)}_{abcd}</math> is type III, <math>C^{(3)}_{abcd}</math> is type II (or II-II) and <math>C^{(4)}_{abcd}</math> is type I.
